'''SYSTAT''' is a graphical [[statistical software]] package.<ref>{{cite news | last=Sandberg-Diment | first=Erik | date=October 7, 1986 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/10/07/science/personal-computers-evaluating-the-crop-of-statistical-software.html | title=Evaluating the Crop of Statistical Software | work=The New York Times | page=C4 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524185114/https://www.nytimes.com/1986/10/07/science/personal-computers-evaluating-the-crop-of-statistical-software.html | archivedate=May 24, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=O'Keeffe | first=Linda | author2=Jay Klagge | date=1986 | url=https://archive.org/details/statisticalpacka00okee/page/87/ | title=Statistical Packages for the IBM PC Family | publisher=McGraw-Hill | page=85–95 | isbn=9780070563209 | via=the Internet Archive}}</ref> It was one of the earliest statistical software ever to be ported for [[personal computer]]s. It was originally developed by [[Leland Wilkinson]] in the late 1970s, who was at the time an [[assistant professor]] of psychology at the [[University of Illinois Chicago]].<ref name=asa>{{cite journal | last=Hilbe | first=Joseph M. | date=May 2008 | url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/27644002 | title=Systat 12.2: An Overview | work=The American Statistician | publisher=American Statistical Association | volume=62 | issue=2 | pages=177–178 | via=JSTOR}}</ref> Wilkinson based SYSTAT loosely off of a statistical software application developed by the [[SAS Institute]] for [[mainframe computer]]s.<ref name=iw>{{cite magazine | last=Fridlund | first=Alan J. | date=September 1, 1986 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cS8EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA33 | title=Systat: Flexibility, Power, Good Support | work=InfoWorld | publisher=IDG Publications | volume=8 | issue=35 | pages=33–35 | via=the Internet Archive}}</ref> He developed the base algorithms starting in the late 1970s<ref name=iw /> and delivered the first version of the software on [[CP/M]] for the [[Cromemco Z-2]] in 1980.<ref name=sageencyc>{{cite book | last=Cunningham | first=Michael R. | date=2022 | doi=10.4135/9781071812082.n618 | chapter=SYSTAT | title=The SAGE Encyclopedia of Research Design | publisher=SAGE Publications | volume=4 | edition=2 | pages=1664-1667 | isbn=9781071812129}}</ref><ref name=macweek>{{cite magazine | last=Custer | first=Linda | date=June 5, 1990 | url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A8519214/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=bookmark-GPS&xid=2b4e6b06 | title=Turning raw data into statistics | work=MacWEEK | publisher=IDG Publications | volume=4 | issue=21 | pages=54 ''et seq''. | via=Gale}}</ref> In order to market SYSTAT, Wilkinson and his wife Ruth Van Demark incorporated Systat Software Inc. in [[Chicago]], Illinois, in 1983. The company eventually grew to over 50 employees.<ref>{{cite book | last=Fiffer | first=Steve | date=1986 | url=https://archive.org/details/soyouvegotgreati00fiff/page/31/ | title=So You've Got a Great Idea | publisher=Addison-Wesley | pages=31–36 | isbn=9780201115369 | via=the Internet Archive}}</ref> After the decline of CP/M, the company ported SYSTAT to [[PC DOS]] in 1984.<ref name=macweek /><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hilbe | first=Joseph | date=February 2005 | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/27643625 | title=A Review of Systat 11 | work=The American Statistician | publisher=American Statistical Association | volume=59 | issue=1 | pages=104–110 | via=JSTOR}}</ref> It was ported to the [[Mac (computer)|Macintosh]] in 1986<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Staff writer | date=October 20, 1986 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gvU799ixIbcC&pg=PA106 | title=New Products/Microcomputers | work=Computerworld | publisher=IDG Publications | volume=XX | issue=42 | page=103–108 | via=Google Books}}</ref>{{rp|106}} and Windows in 1992.<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Low | first=Lafe | date=June 29, 1992 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=blEEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA20 | title=Systat for Windows debuts | work=InfoWorld | publisher=IDG Publications | volume=14 | issue=26 | page=20 | via=Google Books}}</ref>

In 1995, SYSTAT was sold to [[SPSS Inc.]], who marketed the product to a scientific audience under the SPSS Science division. By 2002, SPSS had changed its focus to [[Analytics|business analytics]] and decided to sell SYSTAT to Cranes Software in [[Bangalore]], India. Cranes formed Systat Software, Inc. to market and distribute SYSTAT in the US, and a number of other divisions for global distribution. The headquarters are in San Jose.<ref name=sageencyc /><ref name=asa />

By 2005, SYSTAT was in its eleventh version having a revamped codebase completely changed from [[Fortran]] into [[C++]]. Version 13 came out in 2009, with improvements in the user interface and several new features.<ref name=sageencyc /> On January 15, 2024, SYSTAT was transferred to Grafiti LLC.<ref>{{cite web | date=January 15, 2024 | url=https://systatsoftware.com/ | title=Announcement | publisher=Systat Software | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260513010439/https://systatsoftware.com/ | archivedate=May 13, 2026}}</ref>
